templates.text: Sudden loud clatter → whole-body startle, followed by a sharp, high-pitched cry.
A sharp, high-frequency ring → arms fling outward, head jerks back, breath hitches.
Unexpected door slam → immediate Moro reflex, eyes snap open, then sustained wailing.
Sudden metallic crash → torso arches, limbs stiffen, a loud cry erupts within {seconds} second.
A sudden, deep bang → vigorous startle, face flushes red, cry escalates rapidly.
Abrupt siren wail → head turns toward sound, body tenses, crying begins without pause.
Sharp hand clap → symmetrical limb extension, gasp, then a forceful, rhythmic cry.
Sudden shout nearby → full Moro response, followed by agitated limb cycling and crying.
Unexpected dog bark → eyes widen, arms jerk up, cry starts low and rises sharply.
A piercing alarm tone → body jolts, breathing stops briefly, then a loud, distressed cry.
Sudden, loud percussion → rapid blink, full-body extension, immediate vocal protest.
Crash of falling objects → startle, facial grimace, and a strong, continuous cry for air.
Abrupt, high-decibel noise → autonomic surge: tachycardia, cry, and limb thrashing.
Sharp whistle blast → head retraction, hands splay, a robust cry follows instantly.
Sudden crowd roar → whole-body shudder, followed by intense, coordinated crying and movement.
Unexpected glass shatter → gasp, trunk stiffens, cry emerges loud and clear.
A sudden bass thump → viscerally felt vibration triggers a jolt and immediate vocalization.
Sharp electronic beep → orienting turn toward sound, then a startled cry and limb recoil.
Loud, abrupt laughter → brief freeze, then a full startle reflex and vigorous crying.
Sudden vacuum roar → eyes squeeze shut, body arches, cry builds to a peak over {seconds} seconds.
Crashing cymbal sound → symmetrical arm thrust, leg extension, and a powerful cry.
Unexpected thunderclap → massive startle, autonomic flush, sustained loud wailing.
A sudden, shrill scream → immediate protective flexion, then an explosive cry response.
Abrupt car horn → head and eyes turn toward stimulus, body jolts, cry is instantaneous.
Loud, cracking sound → rapid blink reflex, full Moro, cry integrates with motor agitation.
Sudden fire alarm → orienting pause, then whole-body startle and robust crying effort.
Sharp, staccato noise → breath catch, trunk extension, cry is strong and rhythmic.
Unexpected loud music → startle, facial expression of distress, cry overrides other activity.
A sudden plate smash → auditory-tactile integration: flinch, then a vigorous cry response.
Abrupt, loud argument → stress response: cry, increased muscle tone, and facial flushing.
